title: Write for How Your Customers Really Ask
h1: Write for how your customers really ask
desc: Customers ask full questions in natural language, not keyword lists. Learn where to collect their real questions and how to answer them in your content.
lead: People now ask tools full questions in their own words. If your pages use the words your customers use, they are easier to match and easier to quote.
body:
Search used to reward short keyword phrases. Customers now type or say whole questions: "which accounting software is easiest for VAT in Saudi Arabia?" Your content should be written for that kind of question. This does not replace search basics. It adds a habit: write the answer in the customer's language.

Keywords versus questions

Keyword styleQuestion style
accounting software VATWhich accounting software handles VAT for a small shop?
cake delivery JeddahCan I order a birthday cake for tomorrow in Jeddah?
CRM priceHow much does a CRM cost for a team of five?

The question style includes context: who is asking, what for, in which place. Your page should answer that context.

Where to find the real questions

Do not invent them. Collect the ones people already ask you:

  1. Chat messages. Go through your WhatsApp or Instagram messages from the last two months and copy the questions as written.
  2. Calls and sales meetings. Ask your team which questions come up again and again.
  3. Reviews and comments. Customers explain what confused them or surprised them.
  4. Search Console. If you use it, the Queries report shows what people typed before reaching you.
  5. Your own tests. Ask AI tools the questions and note which follow-ups they suggest.

A note on Arabic and dialects

Many customers in the Gulf ask in their dialect, in Modern Standard Arabic, or in English, sometimes all three. I collect the questions in whatever form they arrive, then write my published content in clear Modern Standard Arabic and use the customers' own terms for products and services. I do not write the page itself in dialect. This is my practice, not a platform rule.

Answer inside the page

Turn each real question into a heading and answer it in the first sentence. This is the habit that changed the most in my work at Qoyod: I rewrote the opening of pages so each began with a short, direct answer. Pages in that project reached page one in under 24 hours. I cannot promise that speed for you. It shows what answer-first can do inside a strong site.

Keep the customer's wording in the heading, then add detail below. Use their term for the product, not your internal name for it.

Group and prioritise

You will collect many questions. Group them by topic, count how often each repeats, and write for the most frequent first. One page, one main question.

Check whether it works

Take ten of the questions and ask them on two or three tools. Record whether your business is mentioned and how it is described. My free visibility test gives you ready questions by business type if you want a starting set. For the idea of writing answer-first, read answer-first content.

Writing in your customers' words helps people and tools understand you. It does not guarantee any placement.
faq: No. Keywords still matter as part of search basics. Add question-style headings and direct answers on top of them.
How many questions should I collect?
Start with twenty to thirty real ones, group them, and write for the most frequent first.
I collect questions in any form, but write published Arabic content in clear Modern Standard Arabic, using the customers' own terms for products and services.
